commit.message:
Fix beckoning gale monster spell display

It was crashing because beckoning gale has a zap without a to-hit, so
can't look up its defense data from a beam. We skip displaying defenses
for spells unless they define it manually, and do so for gale.
Fix typo: recieve -> receive.
Fix typo: seperate -> separate.
Fix typo: Neccropolis -> Necropolis.
Fix spelling.
Spelling: Change AmE Duelist to AusE Duellist

Fix burstshrooms damage display bug (adinsx)

We do this by always setting the summoner_id on monsterinfos, so that
the describe code can tell if it is being summoned. We gate
"get_known_summoner" on MB_SUMMONED so this has no other effect.

Rather than omit the damage for player burstshrooms (as the previous
code intended), we now use the correct damage.

Fix description of protean grace bonus

Fixes #5350

Fix rn++ resist display amount

Fixes #5387

fix: unintentional level vetos due to traps blocking paths

8d147f2 refactored traps but seems to have unintentionally changed the
logic for level vetos. Before, only teleport or dispersal traps would
count for blocking paths but after, all traps would block paths. This
most noticably drastically increased the veto rate of
grunt_spider_rune_island due to web traps which meant that end vault
became much more rare. (It's already about half as rare as its weight
suggests for other reasons)

Return to teleport and dispersal traps being the only traps to block
paths for the purposes of vetoing levels.

Only show forest as awakened within caster's LoS

Trees outside of this can't hit things, and showing them as angry leads
to people thinking they can.

We do this following the existing example of liquefying and similar
effects which are centred on an actor.

Fix a bug with doubly charmed allies (Flugkiller)

When a monster charmed an ally (e.g. a Hep ancestor), and then we
charmed it back, it would end up permanently hostile in the case that
the monster charm wears off first. We fix this by having our charm
cancel out the monster's, which is already what happens we the charms
happen in the other order on an initially hostile monster.

Let wizards create monsters ignoring item sets

orc ; wand of charming was failing in a paralysis game
Alphabetise some switches

Show resists and defenses in spell descriptions

This adds lines for resists and defenses (AC, EV, SH) to detailed spell
descriptions, including where only a portion is blocked.

Where possible, we derive this straight from the spell's zap, but for
zapless spells we duplicate the information instead. The list of spells
to address came from the spells which specify damage in custom ways.

Add a spell flag for "needs a target"

This allows us to stop suggesting Z-casting spells where it won't do
anything because they need targets to be cast.

Make many spells not target warded monsters

We add a flag indicating that a spell only deals direct damage, and do
not count warded monsters as targets in tracers for such spells.
Add a few more words to Crazy Yiuf's vocabulary.
Fix typos.
Fix a couple typos

Fix green colouring of ego-based menu titles.

Do this by capitalising Ego, which bypasses the entry in
dat/defaults/menu_colours.txt that turns all menu titles containing
"ego" green, and which also makes it match the eventual capitalisation
of the first word in such menu titles.
Allow lookup-help searches of missile egos.

Allow determining missile ego w/o an item.

This is so it can be used in lookup-help searches.
Allow lookup-help searches of armour egos.
Allow lookup-help searches of weapon egos.

Add egos.txt to the descriptions database.

This is so it can show up in lookup-help searches.

Remove locale-specific behavior of the soft_item_slot comparator

Used for sorting many inventory menus.

In some locales (such as is true of default Windows installations in North
America, at the very least), isalpha() could return true for values that
would assert when passed to letter_to_index(). They ought to always match
each other exactly.

Fix dropped consumables getting garbage internal item slots (canofworms)

This code wasn't properly updated after consumable inventory was added,
resulting in non-letters being set for the 'last used inventory slot' of
dropped consumables.

In combination with another bug (fixed in the following commit), this could
cause a crash on some locales when trying to use a dropped consumable off
the floor.
Fix indentation.

Fix the resists checked by monster strikes

Monster airstrike was half-resisted by ice, while sleetstrike was
irresistible

Add another unlikely hybrid to artefacts.

Taken from what appears to be an autocomplete error (but a cool one) in:
https://tavern.dcss.io/t/megaprogress-meteorans-0-30/2003/1
Add another unique-related comment to graffiti.
Add another pattern name and glowing adjective.

Fix a crash placing fog_machine vaults via &L (regret-index)

Exactly one of the uses of clear_need_activate() removed in 91f3a8b seemed
to still be necessary, since local vault placement on an existing level
only activated markers on tiles within said vault (and thus didn't clear
the have_inactive_markers property from the entire level).

Fix an Abyss rune vault missing a rune (Ahyangyi)

When bd093b5 made another difficulty balance pass over Abyss rune vaults,
the efforts to regulate the number of ancient / dread liches in
due_evilmike_abyss_rune_seething_liches accidentally gave that a 66%
chance to not actually place a rune, which this commit fixes.

Fix the Vainglory restriction on invis (rypofalem, particleface)

Apparently broken in 6f7dcbef, which prevented radius 0 halos from being
applied. Vainglory needs a radius 0 halo to communicate its limitation
on invis, so we modify the area application to accept such halos. This
doesn't seem like it breaks any existing callers of _apply_area().
Add another Crazy Yiuf line.

Don't let Breathe Rust make clouds on two sides of a wall at once

If the player was standing such that they could see both sides of a wall,
Breathe Rust could place clouds on both of it simultaneously, eg:

...@..
...#..
§§§#§.
§§§#§.
§§§#§.

Instead, use a standard explosion calculation and pick the first X tiles
out of that (which should also match the targeting UI most directly).

Fix multiple oddities with the Breathe Rust targeter (Flugkiller)

The targeter was calculating the 'explosion' of clouds as if the beam
didn't penetrate targets, but still drawing main path of the beam as if it
did, leading to some very odd and inscrutible shapes.

On top of this, tiles that 'might' be in the radius of effect (if the
player's power is insufficient to fill all of radius 2) were overriding
tiles that will definitely be affected (due to being in the beam's path
itself), contributing to 'gaps' in the affected area. I don't think there
are any other beam-based 'explosions' of variable radius in Crawl at the
moment, but this would have affected those as well.

Finally, the targeter was misleading about this ability's capability to
affect wall monsters. Since its only effect is to place clouds, it can't
affect monsters inside walls in any way, and should convey this more
properly.

Let crab form double archery ego

Crabs are our friends and want to have fun. Let your crab shoot a giant gun.

Fix crash with wall monsters and gavotte

They were crashing when being gavotted into the level boundary. Now they
stop there (with no collision)
Fix some mapstat option parsing

Fix a ziggurat entry vault (rypofalem)

When 2a440f7 updated this ziggurat to use ; instead of ', it did not
update the opaque KMASK. This made the area in the middle look
disconnected and prevented the vault from generating.

Fix an overflow vault that never placed (rypofalem)

3b09176 attempted to fix an issue where we occasionally placed this
vault without stairs, but in doing so it made it unplaceable as it falls
foul of the "do not increase dungeon regions" connectivity check. We
have now fixed the stair problem in a more robust way by banning random
stair removal from touching vaults, so we revert this transparent tag.

The other vault in the same commit is fine to stay transparent, because
it is primary and therefore allowed to disconnect the level.

Do not cull random vault stairs

We used to do four passes of stair-culling:
- Redundant (i.e. walkable-between), non-vault
- Redundant vault
- Random non-vault
- Random vault

The last of these is somewhat unsafe; vaults can rely on stairs for
connectivity, and can be opaque so that connectivity checks won't catch
when this fails. So we remove the last pass; when we would have reached
it we now veto the level. Now that the parent commit fixes stair
culling, this veto is vanishingly rare; in fact in a 500 game mapstat
run there were no instances of it that wouldn't have been vetoed later
as the random stair removal disconnected the level.

Cull redundant stairs better

The comments in the _cull_redundant_stairs function state that it
iterates through stairs if there are more than 3, removing some that are
reachable from other stairs by walking. This is very sensible, as it
means that we remove stairs without breaking connectivity.

However, this isn't what it was actually doing. Instead, it was
iterating through the stairs, removing some that share a type of stair
(e.g. "upstair 2") that is reachable from other stairs by walking. This
could cull arbitrary stairs and leave disconnected regions.

Fix listing of sound in features on ?V

SOUND_BACKEND was missing from command.cc

fix sound conditional in initfile.cc

As currently written, all four defines must exist. But three of them are
intended to be platform-specific and it's not really expected that more
than one of them be defined.

Fix marshalling and unmarshalling of stack flags

This fixes a bug introduced in 2985acf whereby the stash always loaded
zeroed flags on reload, which made autoexplore think stashes were
unvisited and revisit them.

Fixes #5369

Fix monster barding pickup logic being inverted

Monsters who were supposed to be able to pick up and wear bardings were the
only species that were explicitly forbidden from doing so. Whoops.

This fixes #5367

Fix FHEIGHT often having no effect (nicolae)

The height of a feature can be set by a vault using FHEIGHT. However,
this would often not work as the height would get accidentally
overridden when placing the Shoals layout or when giving features in
vaults default heights.

Improve setting of water and floor height in Shoals vaults

We were often setting all floors to the same height and all shallow
water squares to the same height. This would cause tides to flood the
whole vault at the same time rather than gradually move in. It would
also cause wave animations to show a wave everywhere in the vault at
once rather than showing a moving wave.

Instead, make floors farther from water higher and shallow water closer
to floors higher.

Rework making sure squares don't get bad flavour during level gen

If a vault places a feature and then level generation replaces the
feature, we need to remove the tile override and also reset the squares
colour.

Unfortunately, we had multiple ways of achieving this. The first way was
that we would call _set_grd to replace the feature. However, some places
that replaced a feature did so by directly altering env.grid and making
sure every where that needed to call _set_grd did was rather hard. The
second way was that we would not show "feat" tile overrides on floor
tiles so that if a squares that had a "feat" tile override was replaced
with a floor the incorrect tile override wouldn't be shown. The third
way was that we would keep track of which features had been placed by
vaults and reset the squares colour after generating the level if the
feature was different from what the vault had placed.

The third way can be adapted to handle resetting tile overrides,
allowing us to remove the first and second ways. However, I haven't yet
allowed floors to show "feat" tile overrides as we still have a few ways
that these can end up incorrect on floors outside of level generation.

Fix a possible A screen crash in wizmode

When you lower your level in wizmode, innate mutations that were gained
from levelling up are not removed. This can cause A's description of future
mutations to attempt to query mutation levels higher than 3 (eg: if a
vine stalker had fangs 3, then lowered their level below 8, the game would
think they would gain fangs 4 at XL 8 and then crash).

Properly cleaning up innate mutations would be nicer, but let's at least
not crash.

Redraw tentacle segments more promptly

This fixes a little flicker on webtiles where we draw the removal of the
old segments before the addition of the new ones.

Don't create a stash at the player's position every time we load any

The default constructor for Stash set its position to the player's, if none
was specified. This was, as far as I can tell, only used when loading
existing stashes from a save file. Which meant that every single stash
loaded would first intialize itself from whatever was at the player's
position before wiping all that out to load the intended data.

This is a bit pointless and wasteful, but also could create odd errors in
some cases. For instance, the lua tables handling portal markers were not
fully loaded before stashes were, which could result in a massive number of
lua errors when loading a save file where the player was on top of a portal
(as every stash on the level would attempt to read from a table for the
marker at the player's feet). This became more obvious after d744bac fully
reset lua state when the game was reset.

Now we only fully initialize a stash if given an in-bounds position and
don't remap (0,0) to the player's location. (As far as I can tell, this was
only used prior to loading, which should overwrite all state anyway.)

This fixes #5363

Make the abyss shift at the same rate in all directions

This removes an incentive to walk North/South rather than East/West in
order to trigger more shifts and find the rune faster. This incentive
was minor compared to the need to avoid danger, but this way nobody has
to think about it.

Move abyssal shift to world_reacts

We previously checked the abyss shift on player movement. This meant
that if a player moved only through less pedestrian means, such as
scrolls of blinking, they could reach the edge of the abyss. This was
bad both because reaching the edge of the infinite abyss is surprising,
and because it was rather buggy there, with the abyss shifting every
turn without recentering the player. So now we check for a shift every
turn.

Kill tentacles via their heads

When we kill a tentacle segment, we now kick the real (non-reset) death
up to the head, and have it clean up all the tentacles. This means that
we consistently process the head death properly. This mostly matters for
eldritch tentacles, where we now grant XP, immediately remove eldritch
portals, give a custom message, and count the monster as vanquished.

We also remove a block of code that looked like it was doing the same
thing, but never fired.

Fixes #5361

Add owned counts to shopping list (particleface)

This is consistent with the change for shops in a221df3
Update credits

Remove you.prev_grd_targ

After getting yet another bug report about the targeting cursor sticking to
things it shouldn't, I am feeling like dfde840 was misguided and that that
it would have been better to cut this code (which had been unknowingly
nonfunctional for a couple of versions) than reenable it.

While I'd thought it would be mildly helpful in a few situations, it's
turning out to have much larger negative effects in more situations than it
would have had positive ones.

(Really, it might be nice to have that sort of memory operate on the basis
of each individual thing being aimed, but it seems tricky to do this (there
is no unified way to refer to spells/abilities/items and there are multiple
things beyond that which use this interface.))

Don't retain cursor memory after casting hellfire mortar (adinsx)

The spot the player aimed hellfire mortar at was being incorrectly
remembered in a way that would force subsequent spells (including direct
projectiles) to also aim there instead of at proper monster targets.

More properly fix eldritch tentacle death cleanup

While 970ca23 fixed an issue with the portal feature not disappearing, by
removing any cleanup from the monster death event itself, if the tentacle
died on another monster's turn (which is likely), the portal would remain
until the end of the player's *next* turn, preventing them from recasting
the spell until then.

Now, the portal will once again close immediately (but should no longer
sometimes leave around portal features either).

Fix an issue with eldritch portals not disappearing

When a tentacle died, we attempted to clear up its portal. However, this
had two issues:
* It only fired if the tentacle was on the portal itself
* It did not clear up the temporary terrain change

These didn't matter when the tentacle dies elsewhere, because the map
marker tick clears up the portal anyway. But the combination of the two
meant that if the tentacle died while on the portal, the portal never
disappeared.

We fix this by not removing the marker at all in this case, leaving the
terrain reversion handled in a single place.

Fix a softlock involving grunt_nemelex_the_gamble

Items marked as 'unobtainable' (currently used *only* in this single vault)
were deliberately not added to the stash tracker. New logic added in
2985acf made the incorrect assumption that if there was a visible item on
the ground, that it would always be added to the stash (resulting in a
crash from trying to add a null pointer to the stash).

However, not adding unobtainable items to the stash tracker had some other
older bugs - most notably that attempting to examine the item on the ground
would fail to see it at all (since the stash is used to construct the
results of xv). ie: If you xv'd an exciting item in this vault, you would
only see floor. This seems clearly incorrect to me.

To be honest, I am not 100% certain the overall value of this flag as used
in a single vault, but as a stopgap measure, I am adding unobtainable items
into the stash tracker and simply hiding them on stash *search*. This
perhaps should be revisited in future.

Don't assert on looking up the description of a flavour without one

monster_info store the attack properties of a monster at the time they
were last seen. This means they can sometimes have attack flavours that
have since been removed.

There is no reason to assert for this situation (and even if we forget to
add a desecription for a new attack flavour, asserting doesn't feel
appropriate here.)
Fix a clang compile warning (Ge0FF)
Unbrace

Hopefully fix cursor for ranged attacks 'sticking' to old dead targets

If you aimed a ranged attack at a monster and it survived, and you aimed it
again and killed it, the next time you tried to fire, the cursor would
snap to the location you last fired at (because it retained memory of the
location as well as the monster, and when the monster was no longer there,
used the location instead).

I think this bug existed prior to dfde840 but that commit fixed a
different bug that allowed this bug to manifest properly.

(...I admit that I am still not 100% sure that this doesn't result in some
other issue since this UI is fairly complicated, but fingers crossed.)
feat: show owned consumable counts in shops
Fix typos.

Fix a crash when xv-ing monsters with a reaching attack and throwing weapon

The throwing weapon would not be seen when first determining layout of the
attack table, and have no range entry for itself. So if the melee attacks
*did* need a range column, it would read past the end of the array for the
throwing weapon's range.

(Instead, just say they have LoS range.)

Fix Exposed increasing *all* damage, including attack damage (rypofalem)

I went to some trouble to route more parts of attacks through
attack::inflict_damage(), so that we could tell what damage came from
attacks or not, and then somehow never actually set the argument added in
962f017 to true there. Whoops...
Fix item stack hilights not displaying in console (Undo)

Grant a monster halo immediately upon stealing a weapon while having none

Just in case you disarm Maurice *before* he swipes your Eos.

Slightly change internal ordering of monster unequipping

As a more thorough fix to follow e5056c4 this makes monster::unequip
directly unlink the item (so that an agrid invalidation won't see it) and
then calls do_unequip_effects() on its own.

The unlinked item must have something done with immediately afterward
(such as destroy it or place it on the grid), but this should currently be
done in all cases as it is, so I *believe* this should be safe.

Fix a test

The MAP_KNOWN_FLAG flag no longer exists, but a test was trying to use
it to set an area as known. Instead use the MAP_SEEN_FLAG flag as this
will work just as well to set an area as known.

Fix artefact and good item markers sometimes not showing

We were using multiple types to store map flags (such as int, uint32_t,
and uint64_t). This resulting in us accidentally clearing the
MAP_MORE_ITEMS_GOOD and MAP_MORE_ITEMS_ARTEFACT flags in
map_cell::set_door_connect as they can't be stored in the uint32_t that
it was using.

Fix out of view toxic bog not disappearing until game reload

When the player moves out of sight of their toxic bog it ends.
However, we weren't redrawing the squares where it had ended so they
wouldn't see this unless they reloaded the game.

Stop-gap measure to stop crashes when killing monsters above lava

A monster dropping equipped items into lava was producing a crash as of
febc422. This should stop said crashes, but will result in incorrect
behavior regarding certain items (such as halo/umbra-granting equipment)
that fall into lava this way.

I am putting a stop-gap measure in place to avoid the most urgent issue
since there are some complexities with fixing this more properly.

Fix unmarshalling 64 bit map flags

We were storing the map flags in an `unsigned int` when unmarshalling
them which caused the MAP_MORE_ITEMS_GOOD and MAP_MORE_ITEMS_ARTEFACT
flags to be lost as they require more than 32 bits to store.

Use latest Windows SDK

Using the old Windows 8.1 SDK was causing MSVC build errors.

Fix being able to use Bestial Takedown while netted (Planckenstein)

Even more comically, it didn't actually interfere with your attacks (since
that is checked outside of melee_attack itself), so you'd just leap around
with this decorative net on top of you.

Fix fortress crab not doubling artprop regen (Mandarbmax)

Due to the unusual way ARTP_REGENERATION is queried (as a consequence of
regen items needing to attune to the player individually, such that we
cannot simply check their combined sum), fortress crab's armour property
doubling wasn't affecting it at all.

(There's probaby a nicer way to structure this that allows
_player_bonus_regen() to use the artprop cache - possibly by specifically
only caching ARTP_REGENERATION off attuned items and calling
you.equipment.update() whenever an item becomes attuned. But I'm leaving
that for another time.)

Mention Exegesis's ability to be recast for cheaper (Midn8)

Mildly awkward given that the ability's name is based on the spell it's
recasting, but hopefully this is at least marginally clearer.
Fix missing -Jolt status description (Dilly)
Mention fortress crab's ability to wield two-handers in one hand (ssm_)
Add another name.

Fix wording.

Consistently use possessives before gerunds.

Fix pronoun.

Gods have no pronouns, not even "they."
Fix wording.

Fix another compiler warning

Since spret::seen_hups was added. (But it's not possible to get that return
value via this code path anyway, I'm fairly sure.)
Fix a couple compiler warnings with the debug version (rypofalem)
Fix tag upgrade build

Edit a pronoun in Goji's description to reduce confusion (apparently)

I was using 'they' in a gender-neutral sense in the last sentence (and
because I felt it had better cadence), rather than as a statement about
Goji's own gender. However, a surprising number of people interpreted it as
inconsistent with the use of he/him earlier in the description and now that
I've seen someone argue that this means Goji must be the name of the
*moth*, I am conceding that maybe I am the weird one in thinking it reads
completely naturally as it is.

Give sphinxes a chance to spawn with a barding

And increase drop rates slightly across the board

Remove an awkward method used to force autopickup

When an item became identified, if its unidentified state had been flagged
for autopickup, a prop was used to force autopickup to remain on after it
was identified.

This had some awkwardnesses, since this prop would *force* autopickup to
remain on for that item, no matter else might later tell it to turn off,
including .rc scripts (such as the one used by default to avoid autopickup
of redundant jewellery), becoming useless at a later time, and even
toggling it off with the autopickup menu.

While in *most* cases, said item would be picked up immediately, sometimes
this was not the case (most commonly with Ash, where you can ID items from
a distance). So if, for instance, you ID'd an rPois ring from a distance,
but were unable to pick it up (perhaps it was in a vault), then found
another rPois ring, the original ring would remain on autopickup forever,
despite the game saying that picking it up was pointless. Similar problems
could happen with an item later becoming literally useless (perhaps due to
gaining a slot-blocking mutation).

While I cannot be certain, I wonder if this may also be the root cause of
a rare-but-recurring bug people have reported with redundant rings being
picked up (which I could never reproduce).

In any case, identification works fairly different now than when this hack
was first added, and I am hoping it's no longer doing anything
load-bearing. (And if it is, then the root cause of that should be
addressed in a better way.)

Pick up missing aux armour by default

This snippet was available in advanced_optioneering.txt for quite a while,
but it's something players have asked about repeatedly and it feels like a
reasonable thing to simply make default now (especially since inventory
space isn't at a premium these days).

Allow Maurice to actually use melee weapons he steals

Maurice can equip and use ranged weapons they steal from the player, but if
they steal a melee weapon, they will just stick it in their secondary
weapon slot and never actually use it (preventing them from ever stealing a
ranged weapon at a later time, in fact.)

He can already pick up and wield melee weapons from the ground, and I'm
pretty sure the original intention of their code was for them to wield
melee weapons they steal (but the function names were misleading at the
time it was first written; see c625362)
